description: Machine-readable requirements registry for the Founder Alpha. Every entry names its original source, the module that implements it, the executable evidence that verifies it, and any known gap. Verified by backend/scripts/requirements/verify_registry.py, which fails closed on a dangling dependency, a missing module, or a 'verified' claim with no existing test behind it. Classes: mandatory_before_private_start = the private start must not happen without it; necessary_for_safe_autonomy = required before MainAI runs unattended for long; required_for_production = needed for a real multi-user deployment; future_optional = deliberately deferred.

requirements.title: A response may only claim execution that a real, persisted job row backs
requirements.source: backend/app/mainai_runtime_contract.py module docstring; founder requirement quoted there
requirements.security_implications: Prevents the model from reporting work it did not do; a claim is only as trustworthy as the row it cites.

requirements.title: At most one worker executes a given job; every write proves it still holds the lease
requirements.security_implications: Lease generation is the fencing token; without it a stale worker can duplicate privileged side effects.

requirements.title: An expired task_execution lease is never silently handed to a second worker
requirements.security_implications: Blind reclaim of a job with real external side effects is duplicate privileged execution.

requirements.title: A dead attempt is recovered through inspect -> classify -> founder-approved takeover, never auto-approved
requirements.security_implications: Recovery must not repeat or silently approve privileged actions that already left the machine.

requirements.title: Lease expiry is judged by the database's own clock, in the columns' own type domain
requirements.security_implications: A skewed app clock either takes over a live privileged attempt (duplicate execution) or never recovers a dead one.

requirements.title: Untrusted AI edits never modify the live checkout; verification runs against the isolated attempt
requirements.security_implications: An unaccepted proposal must never reach the code the next startup executes; the isolated base must not inherit a credential-bearing Git remote.

requirements.title: Every row is isolated per owner by PostgreSQL row-level security
requirements.security_implications: The single-user Founder Alpha still runs multi-tenant code paths; RLS is what makes a cross-owner leak impossible rather than unlikely.

requirements.title: Sessions live in HttpOnly cookies with rotation, revocation and CSRF protection
requirements.security_implications: No token is reachable from JavaScript; a stolen refresh token is single-use and revocable.

requirements.title: The runtime database role cannot truncate, reference or trigger, and cannot touch migration state
requirements.security_implications: A compromised application connection must not be able to erase data wholesale or rewrite the schema revision.

requirements.title: Mandatory, fail-closed security CI with tamper-resistant controls
requirements.security_implications: A check that cannot fail is decoration; the gate must fail on failure, cancellation and silent suppression.
gaps: CodeQL requires GitHub Advanced Security on a private repository; prepared but NOT enforced until an administrator enables it and sets CODEQL_ENABLED=true.
CODEOWNERS review requirement needs branch protection, which requires repository administration.

requirements.title: Capabilities are explicit, least-privilege, and drift between code and declaration fails closed
requirements.security_implications: No actor may merge, deploy, approve its own change or disable a check.
gaps: Runtime enforcement of the denials is by code inspection plus absence of code paths (no merge method exists); there is no separate runtime policy engine.

requirements.title: The database can be backed up, verified and restored with executable proof
requirements.security_implications: A restore path that was never executed is not a recovery plan.
gaps: The scheduled off-host backup destination and its retention policy are founder/deployment decisions, not implemented here.

requirements.title: A crashed attempt is restart-recoverable and never fabricates an outcome
requirements.security_implications: Checkpointing avoids repeating a non-idempotent provider call or push after a crash.

requirements.title: A hung test fails with a named stack instead of hanging the suite
requirements.security_implications: An unbounded hang is an availability failure that also hides the defect that caused it.

requirements.title: Knowledge ingestion, retrieval and grounded answers with citations
requirements.security_implications: Uploaded content is untrusted input; storage blobs are referenced by DB row and never executed.
gaps: End-to-end retrieval quality with the founder's real corpus is not measured here; correctness of the pipeline is, quality of the answers is a product decision.

requirements.title: Persistent memory survives a new session and a restart
requirements.security_implications: Memory is owner-scoped by RLS; a re-authenticated session is a distinct trust boundary.

requirements.title: Local model communication, verified with a real protocol against a real server
requirements.security_implications: The local model must be reachable without any paid egress path being configured.
gaps: Hardware/model deployment for the founder's inference gas is NOT verified by this branch. Only the protocol integration (real HTTP to a local server) is exercised, in the dedicated real-local-AI workflow. Do not read this as 'the model is deployed'.

requirements.title: Multi-user registration, quotas and per-tenant rate limits
requirements.security_implications: Public registration is deliberately disabled for the Founder Alpha; enabling it is a founder decision.
gaps: Public registration is disabled by design for a single-founder deployment; the multi-tenant onboarding flow is out of scope for the private start.

requirements.title: Automatic merge and deployment by MainAI
requirements.security_implications: Deliberately unimplemented: github_client.py has no merge method, so there is no code path this flag could enable.
gaps: No implementation exists and none is planned before the private start. The flag exists so a future implementation has an explicit off-by-default switch.

requirements.title: Privileged operations are gated by explicit, least-privilege capabilities that an agent cannot extend itself
requirements.source: Mission 3 (startup security boundary): 'Verify all critical privileged operations have enforceable capability boundaries'; docs/SECURITY_CONTROLS.md
requirements.security_implications: Capabilities are declared in one manifest, verified in CI against the runtime contract, and the proposal path has no remote and no credential-bearing Git configuration to abuse.

requirements.title: Audit records cannot be silently rewritten — not by an agent, not by a compromised role
requirements.source: Mission 3: 'Ensure audit records cannot be silently rewritten by ordinary agents'; app/models/audit.py docstring claimed immutability with nothing enforcing it
requirements.security_implications: Before 0079 the trail was only documented as immutable: any connection with UPDATE/DELETE could erase its own history. The trigger makes the guarantee survive a compromised application role and even the superuser connection.

requirements.title: Retrieved content is treated as data, and cannot impersonate the operator or escape its fence
requirements.source: Mission 3/6 (malicious retrieved instructions); the chat path previously concatenated document text into the SYSTEM message unfenced
requirements.security_implications: A source document is attacker-controllable. Fencing plus marker defusing stops it from closing the excerpt early and issuing operator-level instructions; the rule is also stated to the model next to the excerpts.

requirements.title: A real local model answers, embeds and fails closed correctly on this hardware
requirements.source: Mission 1: 'Do not confuse mocked socket tests with successful model inference'
requirements.security_implications: Proves the integration boundary is real in both directions: a document that issues orders is contained, and a missing model is reported as a provisioning gap rather than an outage.
gaps: Verified on the founder's Mac against ollama 0.40.16 with qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct and nomic-embed-text; the acceptance tests skip (they do not pass) on CI runners without a model runtime, so CI green does not re-prove inference.
No GPU/model sizing decision has been made for the founder's production hardware; latency measured on this machine is not a capacity claim.

requirements.title: Retrieval quality is measured on a realistic corpus, not asserted from a fixture
requirements.source: Mission 1: 'build realistic multi-document acceptance datasets, evaluate citation accuracy, document isolation, retrieval relevance, and persistence after restart'
requirements.security_implications: Includes an adversarial source and a contradicted draft, and proves a second owner's near-identical document never appears in the first owner's results.
gaps: Measured on an eight-document synthetic corpus: recall@3 1.00, MRR 0.92, citation@1 0.83. The founder's real corpus (hundreds of documents, real duplicates) is not measured yet.

One recorded weakness: for a paraphrased question the contradicted DRAFT outranks the final report because it repeats the phrase more densely — retrieval alone cannot resolve that, the conflict flag is what protects the answer.

requirements.title: A failed attempt is classified and recovered instead of being retried blindly
requirements.security_implications: Recovery never re-grants authority: a taken-over attempt must re-prove its lease generation, and a completed-but-unpushed attempt is never re-executed.

requirements.title: Background work is owner-scoped, cancellable and bounded — it cannot run unbounded
requirements.source: Mission 2: 'Prevent duplicate execution and unbounded background activity'
requirements.security_implications: Cancellation is checked at checkpoints rather than by killing a process mid-write; a cancel requested while a real subprocess runs lets it finish and stops at the next boundary, so no half-applied privileged state exists.

requirements.title: Backups are verifiable and restorable, and corruption is detected before it is trusted
requirements.security_implications: A restore path that trusts a corrupted archive is worse than no restore path: verification happens before restoration is attempted.

requirements.title: A verified backup exists off the host it protects
requirements.source: Mission 1: 'Do not claim off-host retention without actual off-host evidence'
requirements.security_implications: A backup on the same disk survives neither disk loss nor ransomware nor a compromised host — the exact events a founder needs continuity for.
gaps: No off-host destination is configured or tested. The mechanism can produce and verify an archive, but nothing demonstrates it leaving the host.
Destination, retention window and encryption are founder decisions (cost and data-residency), not engineering defaults.

requirements.title: Problems, solutions and decisions can be recorded and revisited through an authorized path
requirements.source: Mission 2 (disconnected modules): app/problem_learning/service.py has no router or worker entry point
requirements.security_implications: The service is deterministic, owner-scoped and makes no provider calls — it is safe to expose, but exposing it defines what MainAI treats as a remembered problem, which is a product decision.
gaps: 786 lines of implemented, owner-scoped learning service that no endpoint or worker reaches: the founder cannot record a problem, approach or decision today.
Wiring it means choosing the surfaces (chat capture? a review screen? both) and what counts as a durable decision — deliberately not decided by this branch.

requirements.title: The composed executive cycle is intentionally dormant until authority is granted
requirements.source: Mission 2: 'Do not connect a dormant privileged module merely to make a coverage metric green'; app/mainai_executive/__init__.py states 'Provider activation remains disabled'
requirements.security_implications: The package plans, looks around and dry-runs, but never authorizes work and never activates a provider. Its own denial list is enforced by test so it cannot be quietly promoted into an authority.
gaps: The cycle is not reachable from any authorized path, by design. Enabling it unattended is exactly the 'first_cycle_go' decision, which stays false.
Scheduling policy (cadence, budget, what it may do without asking) is an open founder decision, not an implementation detail.

requirements.title: A real GitHub push/PR executes only with explicit authorization and never twice
requirements.source: Mission 1 (real GitHub execution): 'Never perform an unauthorized real push'
requirements.security_implications: GITHUB_WRITE_ENABLED gates the path; the write is idempotent by branch/task, and a crash between commit and push is recovered through the takeover pipeline without creating a second PR.
gaps: Exercised against a real local Git repository and a recorded HTTP layer, never against github.com with real credentials — a real push would be a deployment action this branch is not authorized to perform.
Server-side branch protection and required checks for MainAI-authored PRs are repository settings that still need an administrator.
